In nursing school I got assigned a bariatric patient that had been on the floor all summer. His backstory was that he was a 34yo male, brought in by his mother for trouble breathing. He was transported by car, I have NO idea how. She was his primary caregiver as he was 98% bed bound. He presented with pneumonia (in April) and a volleyball sized wound on his back (bedsore) that was so deep his spine was visible.

By the time I saw him in September the wound was the size of a grapefruit. It was the first and only time in nursing school I dry heaved. I was the one who had to unpack his wound, apply cream, and repack it. The sight of the wound was not the issue, the issue was the smell as I was unpacking it. I had to tell him I forgot something, go outside the room to dry heave, and go back in to finish.

I innocently asked the nurse I was working under why he had two belly buttons, one in the normal place and one about 12 inches lower. She smirked and said, "You'll see, come with me." We went in and four people and a lift hoisted him into a semi seated position, and she placed a bed pan and towels under his lower belly button. From about four inches inside, his poor buried penis let out a steam of foul smelling urine. The nurse cleaned up the best she could. There was no scrotum in sight, it was integrated into the lower roll of fat. Think like a smooth section of sand and in the middle you rake lines in a little round section.

However, that was not enough to make me hate fat people. The moment that I turned to the dark side was when I saw his "encouragement board". It was this white board where they would write his goals for the day (sit up 3 times, lift legs 5 times, etc.) If he met his goals there was basically a goddamn party for him. No one was ever allowed to say anything negative to him. He almost constantly threatened to sue the hospital for the lack of care he was receiving. They had had one bariatric bed in the whole hospital, which was being used, so it took 3 days to get a proper bed. Plus, his mom said that the hospital was to blame for some smaller bed sores he got while in the hospital. In addition, they were planning on suing because the first people that took care of him upon admittance were less than friendly (go figure).

This 34yo man was NOT mentally disabled, I had many opportunities to talk to him, and his mentation seemed average. I have no idea how his case ended up, by the time I graduated in December, he was still in the hospital.

The gloom and fear from the battle had not quickly subsided as the Sea Fairers performed their rituals for those that perished. The losses had been great and particularly heavy hitting was the loss of the Love's Devotion. The ship held a special bond to those that were its crew. As the submarines raced along the coasts they stopped occasionally so the remaining sailors could get out in the air and recuperate. The inside of the new ships was crowded and tight. The vines were messier, occasionally springing leaks. In Leviathans fall the vines grew thorns. If they did not surface often enough the thorns grew worse. On one occasion the vines smothered a Sea Farer in his sleep who had been pulling off the thorns that grew beside his hammock.

Mar'dy had lost something too, his dominant hand to a particularly sharp sword. In the arena this spelled death for the weak, if they were more famous they would have a sword arm forged for them, though it was well known that this was just for show. Any moderately trained warrior could out-parry such a thing. Still he considered it, though not with the sword he had taken off the ship. It was simply too high quality to be dismantled for such a purpose.

The Saen had healed him with what little herbs they had. The stump was still sore but new tissue had already grown around it. The abilities of these creatures still fascinated him, though their party was smaller. He mourned the sweet voices of many the shrubs and flowers, though Saule seemed well adjusted to it.

"I talked to them before the battle. They knew what would happened and we made our peace."

Mar'dy was still haunted by the sight of the Naga. The way the ship moved and sounded did not help. It was Leviathan through and through. It seemed to like him, and for whatever reason it was he wasn't sure. He had killed the master of the Leviathan that was consumed to make it. Perhaps it was some sort of appreciation left over from the Love's Devotion. The captain too was well liked, the vines seemed to loosed in her presence. But she still couldn't make the same connection and it wore thin on her.

Mar'dy sat in his quarters for the most part, he hadn't been assigned any duties and was still considered to be injured, though he felt rather well. He shared the small cramped space with the ships cartographer. The old cartographer spent most of his time conversing with Mar'dy. His duties were few and far between, he could not see the land from inside a submersible ship. Mar'dy asked him one day.

"What are those strange scribbles on the map you have?"

"Scribbles? Which ones?" He replied, pulling it out.

"Those right there, and there are some more here."

"Those aren't scribbles, those are letters and words. I suppose our writing must be different than yours."

"Ah. Yes I knew that."

"You can't read can you?" The cartographer said with a grin across his face.

"Well, no. Some Lot'dy can read, actually quite a few of them. They didn't bother teaching me."

"A great shame! Reading is knowledge, its communication. Its what brings people together."

#####[KNAWLIDGE](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IfwfTc-yC1o)

"Perhaps you could to teach me how to."

"Well I lost so many of my books! I still could though if you want. Lets start with the basics..."

And so Mar'dy and the cartographer spent the days they teaching Mar'dy how to read and write. Soon Mar'dy was able to write out the letters, he could sound out words and could read words by sounding them out. The cartographer, seeing that Mar'dy had trouble using a stylus with his non-dominant hand, and the nature of the hands of the Lot'dy, offered a suggestion.

"What do you plan on doing with that stump of yours?"

"Saule is my friend!"

"No, I'm talking about your arm, not the Saen."

"Oh. I'm not sure."

"Well did you want a knife or a hook on it?"

"Not really, no. I am relatively ambidextrous, I wouldn't need such a thing."

"You clearly aren't." He said pointing to Mar'dys practicing sheet, filled with the skewed monstrosities of letters.

"Well not in fine motor skills but-"

"Lets say I build you something that you can use the stylus with. That way you don't just have a useless stump."

"You would do that?"

"Well, I've got some old sextants and some straps of leather. I've been thinking about it for a while I could make something."

"That would be mightily generous of you."

And so the old cartographer put together a series of brass pieces, pieces of strings, pulleys hooks and gears. Mar'dy watched with fascination between his studies as he worked skillfully crafting the prosthetic hand for Mar'dy. The day came when they tried it out. Little hooks were placed behind the scales on Mar'dys forearm, allowing him to move the stylus in any direction, as if he had been holding it in his hand.

"It's really quite wonderful. I'll have to find a stylus just like yours so I can use it." The[ stylus](http://calligraphymasters.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/Deluxe-Golden-3D-Style-Classical-Chinese-Dragons-Playing-with-the-Pearl-Carved-3D-Fountain-Pen-Black-with-Push-in-Style-Ink-Converter-Removable-full-pen-e1435629917890.jpg) it was built for was greatest possession of the cartographer.

"Well it is yours."

"Then... Then you can have my sword." Mar'dy offered, flustered.

"What use do I have of that! I can hardly lift it!" Said the cartographer. "You know how they say the pen is mightier than the sword? Well with both you will be undefeated." The cartographer added with a tear in his eye.

Mar'dy did not have time to say anything back before a familiar voice resonated throughout the ship.

"LAND HO!"

Diospyra sighed deeply. deliberately zoning out the thoughts of the ships. Recent events and her recent reflections were weighing heavily on her mind. The company of the Saen had helped hasten her recollections, slowly, memories of her past life were returning, many happy days in the Forest of Brotherhood.

Such happiness came, always at a price. The Saen were clearly suffering, you didn't need to be able to sense their thoughts to notice. It had been a mistake to drag them along. This should have been a journey she took alone.

Diospyra turned to her reflection. The tree-like figure in the background was clearer now, still merely a faint shadow, but slowly gaining substance. With every memory that returned, the figure gained more substance, and so too came the pain of what she had lost.

She was somewhere out there. She is still lost at the Tree of Life, lost in her own mind. She would need guidance and assistance, for she was still broken.

Wait for me Diospyra, I'll find you, I'll fix you.

That's the least I could do.
